Every money figure must pass the money guard (recommendation, invoice/PO/line amounts, prior short-pays) or the deterministic template is used instead.

vendor_notice.body_md:
**Subject:** Short payment on invoice PS-88214 — shrimp billed above contract price

Hello Protein Supplier accounts receivable team,

We have scheduled payment of **$2,759.60** against invoice PS-88214 dated {{INVOICE_DATE}} ($2,847.60 billed) and are holding **$88.00**.

The invoice bills Shrimp 16/20 IQF 2lb × 10 at $4.12/lb. Clause 4.2 of our Vendor agreement 2026 fixes this item at $3.68/lb through {{CONTRACT_EFFECTIVE_TO}} [1], so the line is payable at $736.00 rather than the $824.00 billed. Under clause 4.6, a price change needs a written amendment countersigned by our controller.

The delivery was received in full, so the hold relates to price only.

Please issue a credit memo for $88.00 against PS-88214. If you believe the billed price is correct, reply with the countersigned amendment and we will review it promptly.

Thank you,
Accounts Payable

explanation.body_md:
**Why PS-88214 is held** — shrimp is billed 12% over the contract price.

- Clause 4.2 of the Protein Supplier agreement fixes Shrimp 16/20 IQF at $3.68/lb through {{CONTRACT_EFFECTIVE_TO}}; the invoice bills $4.12/lb [1].
- The shrimp line is $824.00 against $736.00 expected — outside tolerance, so it cannot post automatically.
- Goods were received in full, so the variance is price only.
- The same variance appeared twice this quarter ($61.60 and $47.20); both short-pays were accepted.

**Recommendation:** short-pay — pay $2,759.60, hold $88.00 (confidence 0.94). The vendor notice cites clause 4.2.
